<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Item 1.&#160;&#160;Business</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Adams Golf, Inc. (together with its subsidiaries, &#8220;we&#8221;, &#8220;us&#8221;, &#8220;Adams Golf&#8221;, or the &#8220;Company&#8221;) designs, assembles, markets and distributes premium quality, technologically innovative golf clubs for all skill levels.&#160;&#160;Our recently launched products include Idea Tech V3 irons and hybrids, Idea a7 and a7 OS irons and hybrids, Speedline Fast 11 and Speedline 9064 drivers, Speedline Fast 11 fairway woods, and Idea Pro Black hybrids and irons.&#160;&#160;We also develop new products under the names of Yes! Putters, Women's Golf Unlimited, the Lady Fairway and Square 2 brands.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We were incorporated in 1987 and re-domesticated in Delaware in 1990.&#160;&#160;We completed an internal reorganization in 1997, and we now conduct our operations through several direct and indirect wholly-owned subsidiaries, agencies and distributorships.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its subsidiaries, all of which are wholly-owned.&#160;&#160;All significant intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Recent Developments</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On January 20, 2011,<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>we<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>closed the acquisition of certain assets of Progear Holdings, Inc. (d/b/a Yes! Golf) (&#8220;Yes! Golf&#8221;)&#160;&#160;upon our payment of $1.65 million.&#160;&#160;The acquisition was pursuant to a U.S. Bankruptcy Court bulk auction sale, and the purchased assets, among other things, the following assets of Yes Golf: (i)&#160;patented putter technology designs, including Yes Golf&#8217;s line of &#8220;C-Groove Putters,&#8221; (ii) registered trademarks and (iii) existing inventory and capital equipment.&#160;&#160;The Company did not assume any of Yes Golf&#8217;s liabilities in connection with the acquisition.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Products</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Adams Golf operates in a single segment within the golf industry (golf clubs and accessories).&#160;&#160;Specifically, we offer multiple classes of products within our business:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Irons</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In August 2010, we launched our Idea Tech V3 line of hybrid iron sets.&#160;&#160;With nickel chromium (NiCr) plated and physical vapor deposition (PVD) black finishes, we believe the ultra-premium clubs establish a new standard in the super game-improvement category by virtue of its technology and design features. Intended for aspiring and recreational players, the Idea Tech V3 set is offered in two configurations (forged or all-hybrid).&#160;&#160;In both the forged and all-hybrid configurations, the eight-piece Idea Tech V3 set consists of 4-, 5- and 6- progressively&#8211;sized hybrids and a 7-mid-hybrid. The forged set features four oversized cavity-back forged irons in 8-iron through gap wedge while the all-hybrid set features four hybrid scoring clubs in 8-iron through gap wedge. The V3 hybrid set won the
Gold designation, the category leader in &#8220;innovation&#8221;, and the Editor&#8217;s Choice award of the 2011 Golf Digest Hot list.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In July 2009, we launched our Idea a7 line of hybrid iron sets and, in August 2009, we launched our Idea a7 OS line of hybrid irons and integrated sets.&#160;&#160;The a7 irons are offered in an eight piece men&#8217;s and senior's sets, with two graphite-shafted hybrid irons integrated into each set.&#160;&#160;The a7 set of irons won a Gold designation in the 2010 Golf Digest Hot List.&#160;&#160;The Idea a7 OS irons are offered in three different eight piece configurations &#8212;one for men, one for women, and one for seniors, all including three hybrids.&#160;&#160;The a7 OS set of irons won a Gold designation in the 2010 Golf Digest Hot List and was also the category leader in &#8220;Performance&#8221; in the iron category.&#160;&#160;We also offer multiple different color versions of the Idea a7 OS
Women&#8217;s integrated set that includes a 460cc titanium driver, fairway woods, a Women&#8217;s Idea a7 OS iron set with three i-woods integrated into the set, a putter and a bag.&#160;&#160;Additionally, we offer the Idea a7 OS Max irons which are offered in an all hybrid eight piece men&#8217;s, women&#8217;s and senior&#8217;s set.&#160;The a7OS Max set of irons won a Gold designation in the 2010 Golf Digest Hot List and was also the category leader in &#8220;Outstanding Innovation&#8221; in the iron category.&#160;&#160;&#160;</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">3</font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Drivers</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We currently offer a variety of different driver models based on the shape, size and material used in the club head.&#160;&#160;The shafts of our drivers are generally graphite.&#160;&#160;During the summer of 2010 we launched the Speedline 9064 drivers and then in January 2011, we launched the fifth generation of Speedline drivers called the Speedline Fast 11 drivers.&#160;&#160;&#160;We continue to use and have further improved upon the patent pending, aerodynamic shape of our drivers, which lessens drag and airflow turbulence and results in faster club head speed and more distance but with a larger footprint as compared to the prior model of Speedline.&#160;&#160; This Fast 11 generation features velocity slot technology, or three visible channels precisely located on the sole and crown to keep the airflow
attached to the club head even longer.&#160;&#160;This technology creates 35 percent less drag and increases club head speed, making the Speedline F11 driver our fastest ever.&#160;&#160;The Speedline family of drivers has already been in the winners' bags at 21 different tour events since introduction in 2009.&#160;&#160;The Speedline Fast 11 driver is offered in standard and draw variations with a variety of lofts and shaft flexes.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Fairway Woods</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During the first quarter of 2011, we launched the Speedline Fast 11 fairway woods.&#160;&#160;Offered in both stainless steel and titanium models, the Speedline fairway woods also feature Velocity Slot Technology.&#160;&#160;This technology has a deep visible channel on both the crown and sole and is designed to increase deflection and reduce stress on the face, thereby expanding the coefficient of restitution, or spring-like effect, for on-center and off-center shots.&#160;&#160;This results in an easy-to-hit fairway wood that, when compared to our prior generation of fairway woods, has a 21 percent improvement in forgiveness across the entire face, better ball speeds and up to 12 yards of increased distance. The Speedline Fast11 fairway woods are offered in standard and draw variations with a variety of lofts and
shaft flexes.&#160;&#160;We offer a variety of individual hybrids in the recently introduced Idea Tech V3 hybrids, Idea a7 and a7 OS, Idea Pro Black, and Idea Tech a4 and a4 OS lines.&#160;&#160;These individual hybrids are designed to be easier to hit than conventional long irons.&#160;&#160;The V3 Hybrid won Gold designation in the 2011 Golf Digest Hot List and was the category leader in &#8220;Innovation&#8221; in the hybrid category.&#160;&#160;The Idea a7 and a7 OS hybrid irons won a Gold designation in the 2010 Golf Digest Hot List and were the category leader in &#8220;Innovation&#8221; in the hybrid category.&#160;&#160; Additionally, Adams Golf hybrids were the most played hybrids on the 2011 PGA, Nationwide and Champions tours combined.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Wedges and Other</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As a complement to the Idea irons, we offer the Tom Watson signature wedges and the Puglielli wedges.&#160;&#160;During the first quarter of 2011, we purchased the assets of Yes Golf.&#160;&#160;We plan to continue the brand and create future products under the "Yes!" name as manufactured by Adams Golf.&#160;&#160;We also offer a line of golf bags, hats and other accessories.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div>&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Design and Development</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our design and development team is responsible for developing, testing and introducing new technologies and product designs.&#160;&#160;This team is currently led by Tim Reed, Vice President-Research and Development.&#160;&#160;Prior to joining our company, Mr. Reed spent over 18 years in the golf industry and, most notably, was responsible for all new product introductions at TearDrop Golf Company, which included TearDrop Putters and Tommy Armour and Ram brand golf clubs.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Together with management, the design and development team engages in a four-step process to create new products.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Market Evaluation -</font> Prior to development of any potential concepts, our management team, in conjunction with the design and development team, performs an evaluation of the current golf market to determine which particular product classes we will pursue for concept development.&#160;&#160;As a part of the market evaluation, we analyze our current product offerings against current and anticipated competitor products with respect to consumer preferences.&#160;&#160;To attempt to determine consumer preferences, we utilize our independent sales force, consumer surveys and market intelligence tools that solicit product and design characteristics desired by consumers.&#160;&#160;Once the consumer product and design characteristics are determined and evaluated,
management and the design and development team determine the product classes and types of products that will be pursued for the upcoming season.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Performance Characteristics -</font> For the product classes and the types of products to be offered within those classes, management evaluates the target market for our new concepts and the performance characteristics that are commensurate with the target market.&#160;&#160;Performance characteristics are always predicated on producing high quality, high performance products.&#160;&#160;Certain performance characteristics that are evaluated include easy playability, ball flight and spin objectives, desired weight and feel of the product and conformity to U.S. Golf Association ("USGA") golf equipment standards.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Patent Review</font> - We consider patent protection for our technologies and product designs to be an important part of our development strategy; however, we may elect not to seek patent protection for some of our technologies or product designs.&#160;&#160;Prior to developing new products, we conduct a search of prior art and existing products to determine whether a new product idea may be covered by an existing patent.&#160;&#160;Patent review, depending upon the complexity of the design involved, generally requires between one and six months to complete; however, this stage of product development typically occurs in conjunction with the development steps of the design and development process.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Development -</font> Concurrent with the patent review process, the design and development team begins to develop computer generated working designs incorporating the desired performance characteristics, which are then modeled using in-house rapid prototyping systems.&#160;&#160;During the development phase, substantial consideration is also given to optimal shaft performance, cosmetics and sound characteristics.&#160;&#160;Once prototypes are developed, they are subjected to stringent iterative testing requirements to determine if the product will deliver the desired performance.&#160;&#160;In certain circumstances, prototypes are distributed to consumers to solicit feedback with respect to specific product performance characteristics and consumer
perception.&#160;&#160;Using consumer feedback, subsequent modifications are made to the products to achieve the performance requirements desired by the identified target market.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Historically, the entire process from Market Evaluation through Development has taken from six to twelve months to complete.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our research and development expenses were approximately $2,551,000, $2,816,000 and $3,758,000 for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and&#160;&#160;2008, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">5</font></div>

<div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
<hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">

<div>&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Patents</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our ability to compete effectively in the golf club market may depend on our ability to maintain the proprietary nature of our technologies and products.&#160;&#160;As of February 22, 2011, we held 67 U.S. patents relating to certain products and proprietary technologies and we had 21 patent applications pending.&#160;&#160;We expect that the 67 currently issued patents will expire on various dates between 2011 and 2026.&#160;&#160;We hold patents with respect to the design and/or utility of various products lines.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Despite our efforts to protect our patent and other intellectual property rights, unauthorized parties have attempted, and are expected to continue to attempt, to copy all, or certain aspects of, our products.&#160;&#160;Policing unauthorized use of our intellectual property rights can be difficult and expensive, and while we generally take appropriate action whenever we discover any of our products or designs have been copied, knock-offs and counterfeit products are a continuing problem in the performance-oriented golf club industry.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that our means of protecting our patent and other intellectual property rights will be adequate.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For risks relating to our patents, see below, &#8220;Risks Associated with Intellectual Property Protection&#8221; contained in Item 1A.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Raw Materials, Manufacturing and Assembly</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We manage all stages of manufacturing, from sourcing to assembly, in order to maintain a high level of product quality and consistency.&#160;&#160;We establish product specifications, select the materials used to produce the components and test the specifications of components we receive.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As part of our quality control program, we review the quality assurance programs at the manufacturing facilities of our component part suppliers to monitor adherence to design specifications.&#160;&#160;In addition to the quality assurance conducted by the suppliers at their facilities, we also conduct random sampling and perform testing of products received from the suppliers, or produced at our facility, to ensure consistency with our design specifications. Golf clubs are then built by our assembly personnel using the appropriate component parts.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have put into place a purchasing procedure that strives to negotiate effective terms with various vendors while continuing to ensure the quality of our components.&#160;&#160;We are frequently re-evaluating existing vendors and testing potential new vendors for the various product lines we offer.&#160;&#160;At any time, we may purchase a substantial majority of our volume of a specific component part from a single vendor, but we strive to maintain primary and secondary suppliers for each component part.&#160;&#160;Substantially all of our iron, fairway wood, driver, hybrids, wedge and putter component parts are manufactured in China, and a significant portion of our inventory purchases are from one supplier in China.&#160;&#160;We purchased approximately 27% and 45% of our total inventory purchased for the years
ended December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively, from this one Chinese supplier.&#160;&#160;</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Marketing</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The goals of our marketing efforts are to build our brand identity and drive sales through our retail distribution channels.&#160;&#160;To accomplish these goals, we currently use golf-specific advertising, engage in promotional activities, and capitalize on our relationships with professional golfers.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Endemic Advertising - </font>Our primary advertising efforts focus on golf-specific advertising, which include advertising with television commercials that run during golf tournaments and advertising in golf-related magazines and certain newspapers.&#160;&#160;We also sponsor developmental professional tours and selected golf tournaments.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Promotional Activities</font> - We engage in a variety of promotional activities to sell and market our products.&#160;&#160;Such activities have included consumer sweepstakes and promotional giveaways with certain purchases.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Relationships with Professional Golfers</font> &#8211; We have entered into endorsement contracts with professional golfers on the PGA, Champions PGA, Nationwide and LPGA Tours and believe that having a presence on these tours promotes the image of our product lines and builds brand awareness.&#160;&#160;On the PGA Tour we have entered into endorsement agreements with professionals such as Ryan Moore, Chad Campbell, Aaron Baddeley, and several others.&#160;&#160;On the Champions Tour, we have entered into endorsement agreements with Tom Watson, Bernard Langer, Tommy Armour III, Paul Azinger and several others.&#160;&#160;On the LPGA Tour, we have entered into endorsement agreements with Yani Tseng, Brittney Lincicome, Brittany Lang, and several others.&#160;&#160;On

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Markets and Methods of Distribution</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our net sales are primarily derived from sales to on- and off- course golf shops, sporting goods retailers, mass merchants and, to a lesser extent, international distributors.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Sales to Retailers</font> - We sell a majority of our products to selected retailers.&#160;&#160;We believe our selective retail distribution strategy helps our retailers maintain profitable margins and maximize sales of our products.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, sales to U.S. specialty retailers, mass merchants, sporting goods retailers, and on course accounts accounted for approximately 81%, 80% and 80%, respectively, of our total net sales.&#160;&#160;As products mature, they may be sold to alternative channels of distribution, which are not in direct competition with selected retailers for premier product lines.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We maintain a field sales staff that, as of February 22, 2011, consisted of&#160;62 independent sales representatives, one senior vice president, one U.S. national sales vice president, one Intl sales vice president, one regional vice president, one regional sales director and two regional sales managers, who are in regular contact with our retail accounts (approximately 4,000 retailers).&#160;&#160;These sales representatives, sales managers and regional vice presidents are supported by eleven inside sales representatives who maintain contact with our retailers nationwide.&#160;&#160;The inside sales representatives also serve in a customer service capacity because we believe that superior customer service can significantly enhance our marketing efforts.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">International Sales</font> - International sales are made primarily in Canada, Europe, South Africa, Japan and other Asian regions.&#160;&#160;International sales in Canada are made through an agency relationship, while sales to other countries throughout the world are made through a network of approximately 36 independent distributors.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008, international sales accounted for approximately 19%, 20% and 20%, respectively, of our net sales.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Website -</font> We maintain a website at www.adamsgolf.com, which allows the visitor to access certain information about our products and heritage, locate retailers, inquire into careers, access corporate information related to corporate governance and news releases, and inquire about contacting us directly.&#160;&#160;We also maintain <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">www.yesgolf.com</font>, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">www.ladyfairway.com</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">www.squaretwo.com</font> for information about our Women's Golf Unlimited product lines.&#160;&#160;We do not currently sell our products via our websites.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Unauthorized Distribution and Counterfeit Clubs</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Despite our efforts to limit our distribution to selected retailers, some quantities of our products have been found in unapproved outlets or distribution channels, including unapproved retailers conducting business on common Internet auction sites.&#160;&#160;The existence of a "gray market" in our products can undermine the sales of authorized retailers, our agents and our foreign wholesale distributors who promote and support our products and can injure our image in the minds of our customers and consumers in general.&#160;&#160;We make efforts to limit or deter unauthorized distribution of our products, but do not believe the unauthorized distribution of our products can be totally eliminated.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In addition, we are occasionally made aware of the existence of counterfeit copies of our golf clubs, particularly in foreign markets.&#160;&#160;When practical, we take action in these situations through local authorities and legal counsel.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Industry Specific Requirements</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We perform ongoing credit evaluation of our wholesale customers' financial condition and generally provide credit without the requirement of collateral from these customers.&#160;&#160;We measure each customer's financial strength using various key aspects such as, but not limited to, the customer's overall credit risk (via Experian and Dun and Bradstreet reports), payment history, industry communications, the portion of the customer&#8217;s balance that is past due and other various items.&#160;&#160;We also look at the overall aging of the receivables in total and relative to prior periods to determine the appropriate reserve requirements.&#160;&#160; Periods will fluctuate depending on the strength of the customers and the change in mix of customer and their respective strength could affect the reserve
disproportionately compared to the total change in the accounts receivable balance.&#160;&#160;We believe we have adequate reserves for potential credit losses, but we cannot be sure how the current global economic recession and credit crisis will affect our customers and in turn, our reserves for potential credit losses.&#160;&#160;Due to industry sensitivity to consumer buying trends and available disposable income, we have in the past extended payment terms for specific retail customers.&#160;&#160;Issuance of these terms (i.e. greater than 30 days or specific dating) is dependent on our relationship with the customer and the customer's payment history.&#160;&#160;Payment terms are extended to selected customers typically during off-peak times in the year in order to promote our brand name and to assure adequate product availability and often coincides with planned promotions or advertising campaigns.&#160;&#160;Although a significant amount of our sales are not affected by these
terms, the extended terms do have a negative impact on our financial position and liquidity.&#160;&#160;We expect to continue to selectively offer extended payment terms in the future, depending upon known industry trends and our financial condition.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In addition to extended payment terms, the nature of the industry also requires that we carry a substantial level of inventory due to the lead times associated with purchasing components overseas coupled with the seasonality of customer demand.&#160;&#160;Our inventory balances were approximately $27,088,000 and $19,721,000 at December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively.&#160;&#160;The increase in inventory levels over this period was primarily a result of improved inventory delivery; during 2009 we experienced delays in product delivery.&#160;&#160;A significant portion of our inventory purchases are from suppliers who are located predominately in China.&#160;&#160;We do not anticipate any changes in the relationships with our suppliers; however, if such changes were to occur, we believe we would have alternative
sources available, although replacing product could take six to nine months.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Major Customers</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are currently dependent on three customers, which collectively comprised approximately 28.9% of net revenues for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;Of these customers, two customers represented greater than 5% but less than 10% of net revenues for the year ended December 31, 2010, and one customer represented greater than 10% but less than 20% of net revenues, while no customers represented greater than 20% of net revenues for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;&#160;For the year ended December 31, 2009, two customers comprised approximately 23.5% of net revenues.&#160;&#160;Of these customers, one represented greater than 5% but less than 10% of net revenues and one customer represented greater than 10% but less than 20% of net revenues and no customers represented greater than 20% of net
revenues for the year ended December 31, 2009.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Seasonality and Quarterly Fluctuations</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Golf generally is regarded as a warm weather sport, and net sales of golf equipment have been historically strongest for us during the first and second quarters.&#160;&#160;In addition, net sales of golf clubs are dependent on discretionary consumer spending, which may be affected by general economic conditions such as the current economic downturn.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we believe that period-to-period comparisons of our results of operations should not be relied upon as an indication of future performance.&#160;&#160;In addition, the results of any quarter are not indicative of results to be expected for a full fiscal year.&#160;&#160;As a result of fluctuating operating results or other factors discussed in this report, in certain future quarters our results of operations may be below the expectations of public
market analysts or investors.&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Backlog</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The amount of our order backlog at any particular time is affected by a number of factors, including seasonality and scheduling of the manufacturing and shipment of products.&#160;At February 22, 2011, we had current backorders of $1,528,000, or 1.8% of total net sales for the year ended December 31, 2010, and orders to be fulfilled at a future date, not to exceed the current year, of $17,929,000, or 20.8% of total net sales for the year ended December 31, 2010.&#160;&#160;At February 22, 2010, we had current backorders of $2,345,000, or 3.1% of total net sales for the year ended December 31, 2009, and orders to be fulfilled at a future date, not to exceed the current year, of $16,934,000, or 22.2% of total net sales for the year ended December 31, 2009.&#160;&#160;The year over year backorder is slightly decreased
primarily a result of better inventory availability currently as compared to prior year.&#160;&#160;The balance is comprised of various product lines including Speedline Fast 11, Idea a7 and a7 OS sets and hybrids, Idea Tech V3 sets and hybrids and integrated sets.&#160;&#160;Future orders have increased as a result of continued forward looking planning by select retailers as well as, increased overall demand from the retailers as we are entering the golf season and increased product demand. &#160;We do not anticipate that a significant level of orders will remain unfilled within the current fiscal year.&#160;&#160; In addition, we believe that the amount of our backlog is an unreliable indicator of future sales levels.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Competition</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The golf club market is highly competitive.&#160;&#160;We compete with a number of established golf club manufacturers, some of which have greater financial and other resources than us.&#160;&#160;Our competitors include Callaway Golf Company, adidas-Salomon AG (Taylor Made - adidas Golf), Nike, Inc. (Nike Golf), Fortune Brands, Inc. (Titleist) and Karsten Assembly Company (PING), among others.&#160;&#160;We compete primarily on the basis of performance, brand name recognition, quality and price.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">&#160;</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For risks relating to Competition, see below, &#8220;Increasing Competition&#8221; contained in Item 1A.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Domestic and Foreign Operations</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Domestic and foreign net sales for the years ended December 31, 2010, 2009 and 2008 were comprised as follows:</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At February 22, 2011, we had 129 full-time employees including 33 engaged in production and quality control, 19 in order fulfillment, 19 in research and development, 11 in sales support, 24 in sales and marketing and 23 in management and administration.&#160;&#160;Our employees are not unionized.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font id="TAB2" style="LETTER-SPACING: 9pt">&#160;&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Item 1A. Risk Factors.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The financial statements contained in this report and the related discussions describe and analyze our financial performance and condition for the periods indicated. For the most part, this information is historical.&#160;&#160;Our prior results are not necessarily indicative of our future performance or financial condition.&#160;&#160;We, therefore, have included in this report a discussion of certain factors which could affect our future performance or financial condition. These factors could cause our future performance or financial condition to differ materially from our prior performance or financial condition or from our expectations or estimates of our future performance or financial condition.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

</div>

<div>&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Continued Uncertainty in the Economy and Impact on Consumers and Retail</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our operations and performance depend significantly on worldwide economic conditions and their impact on levels of discretionary consumer spending, which remain at depressed levels.&#160;&#160;Certain factors that could influence the levels of consumer spending include, but are not limited to, conditions in the residential real estate and mortgage markets, labor and healthcare costs, access to credit, fuel and energy costs, consumer confidence and other macroeconomic factors affecting consumer spending behavior.&#160;&#160;These and other economic factors could have a material adverse effect on demand for our products and on our financial condition and operating results.&#160;&#160;Any&#160;future decrease in economic activity in the United States or in other regions of the world in which we do business could
significantly and adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition in a number of ways.&#160;&#160;Any decline in economic conditions may reduce the purchases of our products, thereby reducing our revenues and earnings.&#160;&#160;Bankruptcies or similar events by retailers and suppliers may cause us to incur bad debt expense at levels higher than historically experienced and could negatively impact overall revenues.&#160;&#160;Credit risk includes the risk that our retail customers will not pay their bills, which may lead to a reduction in liquidity and an eventual increase in bad debt.&#160;&#160;Our retail customers&#8217; credit risk is determined by numerous factors including, but not limited to, each individual customer&#8217;s business borrowings and credit availability, the overall level of economic activity in our various markets and the prices of products and services provided.&#160;&#160;Additionally, increased promotional and closeout activity by our
competitors could adversely impact the health of our customers and increase our credit risk.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Source of Supply</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A significant portion of our inventory purchases are from one supplier in China; we purchased approximately 27% and 45% of our total inventory purchased for the years ended December 31, 2010 and 2009, respectively, from this one Chinese supplier.&#160;&#160;Substantially all of our fairway wood, driver, iron, i-wood, wedge and putter component parts are manufactured in China and Taiwan.&#160;&#160;We could, in the future, experience shortages of components for reasons including but not limited to the supplier&#8217;s production capacity or materials shortages, or periods of increased price pressures, or bankruptcy or similar material adverse effect on its operations and business, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial position and/or liquidity.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Concentration of the Company&#8217;s Customer Base</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Although no one customer that distributes our products accounted for more than 20% of our revenues in 2010, several of our customers still represent a large portion of our revenues each year and the loss of one or more of our top customers could have a significant negative impact on the Company&#8217;s performance.&#160;&#160;For the year ended December 31, 2010, one customer represented greater than 10% but less than 20% of net sales.&#160;&#160;Any decline in or loss of business or the inability of this customer or any of our other large customers to timely pay their obligations, could have a materially adverse effect upon our net sales and financial performance.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Dependence on New Product Introductions; Uncertain Consumer Acceptance</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our ultimate success depends, in large part, on our ability to successfully develop and introduce new products widely accepted in the marketplace.&#160;&#160;Historically, a large portion of new golf club technologies and product designs have been met with consumer rejection.&#160;&#160;Certain products we previously introduced have not met the level of consumer acceptance anticipated by management.&#160;&#160;No assurance can be given that our current or future products will be met with consumer acceptance.&#160;&#160;Failure by us to timely identify and develop innovative new products that achieve widespread market acceptance would adversely affect our continued success and viability.&#160;&#160;Additionally, successful technologies, designs and product concepts are likely to be copied by
competitors.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, our operating results could fluctuate as a result of the amount, timing, and market acceptance of new product introductions by us or our competitors.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;If we are unable to develop new products that will ultimately be widely accepted by customers, it will have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations.&#160;&#160;</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div>&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The design of new golf clubs is also greatly influenced by the rules and interpretations of the USGA.&#160;&#160;Although the golf equipment standards established by the USGA generally apply only to competitive events sanctioned by the organization, we believe that it is critical for our future success that new clubs we introduce comply with USGA standards.&#160;&#160;We invest significant resources in the development of new products and efforts to comply with USGA standards may hinder or delay development of products and adversely effect revenues and customer demand.&#160;&#160;Additionally, increased costs associated with complying with USGA standards could reduce margins and adversely affect the results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Possible</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Decreasing Amount of Golf Played by Consumers</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our revenues are completely driven from sales of golf related products and the demand for these products is directly related to the number of golfers and rounds of golf being played each year and the overall popularity of golf.&#160;&#160;Golf products are recreational in nature and are therefore discretionary purchases for customers.&#160;&#160;Consumers are generally more willing to make discretionary purchases of golf products during favorable economic conditions and when consumers are feeling confident and prosperous.&#160;&#160;If there was a decrease in consumer spending and increase in unemployment, golfers may decrease the number of rounds they play as well as the amount of golf-related products they purchase.&#160;&#160;If golf participation or the number of rounds of golf played decreases, sales of our
products may be adversely affected.&#160;&#160;</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Increasing</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Competition</font></font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The golf club market is highly competitive.&#160;&#160;We compete with a number of established golf club manufacturers, some of which have greater financial and other resources than we have.&#160;&#160;Our competitors include Callaway Golf Company, adidas-Salomon AG (Taylor Made - adidas Golf), Nike, Inc. (Nike Golf), Fortune Brands, Inc. (Titleist) and Karsten Assembly Company (PING), among others.&#160;&#160;We compete primarily on the basis of performance, brand name recognition, quality and price.&#160;&#160;We believe that our ability to market our products through multiple distribution channels, including on- and off- course golf shops and other retailers, is important to the manner in which we compete.&#160;&#160;The purchasing decisions of many golfers are often the result of highly subjective preferences,
which can be influenced by many factors, including, among others, advertising, media, promotions and product endorsements.&#160;&#160;These preferences may also be subject to rapid and unanticipated changes.&#160;&#160;We could face substantial competition from existing or new competitors who introduce and successfully promote golf clubs that enjoy technological advantages or achieve market acceptance.&#160;&#160;Such competition could result in significant price erosion, lower sales, or increased promotional expenditures, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business, operating results and/or financial condition.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that we will be able to compete successfully against current and future sources of competition or that our business, operating results and/or financial condition will not be adversely affected by increased competition in the markets in which we operate.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The golf club industry is generally characterized by rapid and widespread imitation of popular technologies, designs and product concepts.&#160;&#160;Due to the success of the Tight Lies fairway woods, several competitors have introduced similar products.&#160;&#160;More recently, several competitors have introduced hybrid iron sets that compete directly with our hybrid irons sets.&#160;&#160;Should our recently introduced product lines achieve widespread market success, it is reasonable to expect that our current and future competitors would move quickly to introduce similar products that would directly compete with the new product lines.&#160;&#160;We may face competition from manufacturers introducing other new or innovative products or successfully promoting golf clubs that achieve market
acceptance.&#160;&#160;The failure to successfully compete in the future could result in a material deterioration of customer loyalty and our image, and could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, financial position and/or liquidity.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The introduction of new products by us or our competitors can be expected to result in closeouts, promotions or other discounting of existing inventories at both the wholesale and retail levels.&#160;&#160;Such closeouts, promotions or discounting are likely to result in reduced margins on the sale of older products, as well as reduced sales of new products given the availability of older products at lower prices.&#160;&#160;As the Idea Tech V3 product line of irons and the Speedline F10 product lines were launched in 2010, older product lines such as Idea a3 and a3 OS irons and Idea Tech a4 and a4 OS irons and drivers experienced reductions in price at both wholesale and retail levels.</font></div>

<div>&#160;</div>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Risks Associated with Intellectual Property Protection</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Imitation of popular club design is widespread in the golf industry.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that competitors, many of whom have substantially greater resources than we do and have made substantial investments in competing products, will not be able to successfully sell golf clubs that imitate our products without infringing on our copyrights, patents, trademarks or trade dress, or apply for and obtain patents that will prevent, limit or interfere with our ability to make and sell our products.&#160;&#160;There are numerous patents held by third parties that relate to products competitive to us.&#160;&#160;There is no assurance that these patents would not be used as a basis to challenge the validity of our patent rights to limit the scope of our patent rights or to limit our ability to obtain
additional broader patent rights.&#160;&#160;A successful challenge to the validity of our patents may adversely affect our competitive position.&#160;&#160;Moreover, there can be no assurance that such patent holders or other third parties will not claim infringement by us with respect to current and future products.&#160;&#160;Because U.S. patent applications are held and examined in secrecy, it is also possible that presently pending U.S. applications will eventually issue with claims that may be infringed by our products or technologies.&#160;&#160;We have had to defend against infringement claims in the past and the defense and prosecution of patent suits is costly and time consuming, even if the outcome is favorable.&#160;&#160;This is particularly true in foreign countries where the expenses associated with such proceedings can be prohibitive.&#160;&#160;Litigation in respect to patents or other intellectual property matters, whether with or without merit, could be
time-consuming to defend, result in substantial costs and diversion of management and other resources, cause delays or other problems in the marketing and sales of our products, or require us to enter into royalty or licensing agreements, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our business, operating results and financial condition.&#160;</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">There can be no assurance as to the degree of protection afforded by these or any other patents we hold or as to the likelihood that patents will be issued from the pending patent applications.&#160;&#160;Moreover, our patents may have limited commercial value or may lack sufficient breadth to adequately protect the aspects of our products to which the patents relate.&#160;&#160;The U.S. patents we hold do not preclude competitors from developing or marketing products similar to our products in international markets.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our attempts to maintain the secrecy of our confidential business information, include but are not limited to, engaging in the practice of having prospective vendors and suppliers sign confidentiality agreements when producing components of new technology.&#160;&#160;No assurance can be given that our confidential business information will be adequately protected in all instances.&#160;&#160;The unauthorized use of our confidential business information could adversely affect us.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Uncertainty Regarding Continuation of Profitability</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">While we generated net income in each of the five fiscal years from 2003 to 2007 and again in 2010, we were not profitable for the years ending December 31, 2009 or 2008, nor consistently prior to the fiscal year of 2003, and we experienced significant losses prior to the year ended December 31, 2003.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that we will be able to increase or maintain revenues or continue such profitability on a quarterly or annual basis in the future.&#160;&#160;An inability to continue to operate profitably could jeopardize our ability to develop, enhance, and market products, retain qualified personnel, and take advantage of future opportunities or respond to competitive pressures.</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Need for Additional Capital and Market Volatility</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">No assurances can be given that we will have sufficient cash resources beyond twelve months or that we will be able to fund our operations over a length of time. Historically, we have funded capital expenditures for operations through cash flow from operations.&#160;&#160;To the extent our cash requirements or assumptions change, we may have to raise additional capital and/or further curtail our operating expenses, including further operational restructurings.&#160;&#160;If we need to raise additional funds through the issuance of equity securities, the percentage ownership of the stockholders of our Company would be reduced and/or such equity securities could have rights, preferences or privileges senior to our Company's common stock.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Given the current market price for our common stock and the state of the capital markets generally, we do not expect that we would be able to raise funds through the issuance of our capital stock in the foreseeable future at commercially favorable terms, and we may also find it difficult to secure additional debt financing beyond our current credit facility.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurance that financing will be available if needed or if available on terms favorable to us, or at all.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, it is possible that our only sources of funding will be current cash reserves, projected cash flows from operations and up to $15.0 million of borrowings available under our revolving credit facility, assuming that such revolving credit facility continues to be available and that we continue to meet the
covenants and conditions precedent to borrowing, which cannot be assured.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Dependence on Key Personnel and Endorsements</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our success depends to an extent upon the performance of our management team, which includes our Chief Executive Officer and President, Oliver G. (Chip) Brewer, III, who participates in all aspects of our operations, including product development and sales efforts.&#160;&#160;The loss or unavailability of Mr. Brewer could adversely affect our business and prospects.&#160;&#160;In addition, Mr. Tim Reed joined the management team in 2000 in the capacity of Vice President of Research and Development.&#160;&#160;If Mr. Reed is unable to continue to lead his team to develop innovative products, it could also adversely affect our business.&#160;&#160;With the exception of our Chairman of the Board of Directors, B.H. (Barney) Adams, Mr. Brewer, Mr. Reed, Mrs. Pamela High, Chief Financial Officer, and Mr. Brad Barnett,
V.P. of Global Operations, none of our Company's officers and employees are bound by employment agreements, and the employment of such officers and employees is, therefore, at will.&#160;&#160;We established key-men life insurance policies on the lives of Mr. Brewer and Mr. Reed; however, there can be no assurance that the proceeds of these policies could adequately compensate us for the loss of their services.&#160;&#160;In addition, there is strong competition for qualified personnel in the golf club industry, and the inability to continue to attract, retain and motivate other key personnel could adversely affect our business, operating results and/or financial condition.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On the PGA Tour we have entered into endorsement agreements with professionals such as Ryan Moore, Chad Campbell, Aaron Baddeley, and several others.&#160;&#160;On the Champions Tour, we have entered into endorsement agreements with Tom Watson, Bernard Langer, Tommy Armour III, Paul Azinger and several others.&#160;&#160;On the LPGA Tour, we have entered into endorsement agreements with Yani Tseng, Brittney Lincicome, Brittany Lang, and several others.&#160;&#160;On the Nationwide tour, we have agreements with various players.&#160;&#160;All of the above contracts have various dates of expiration through 2013 and require the use of certain of our products.&#160;&#160;The loss of one or more of these endorsement arrangements could adversely affect our marketing and sales efforts and, accordingly, our business,
operating results and/or financial condition.&#160;&#160;From time to time, we negotiate with and sign endorsement contracts with either existing or new tour players.&#160;&#160;As is typical in the golf industry, generally the agreements with these professional golfers do not necessarily require that they use exclusively our golf clubs at all times during the terms of the respective agreements, including, in certain circumstances, at times when we are required to make payments to them.&#160;&#160;The failure of certain individuals to use our products on one or more occasions can result in, and has resulted in, negative publicity.&#160;&#160; Alternatively, poor decisions by professionals sponsored by us could result in negative publicity.&#160;&#160;No assurance can be given that our business would not be adversely affected in a material way by such negative publicity or by the failure of our known professional endorsers to carry and use our products.</font></div>


<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Effectiveness of our Marketing Strategy</font></div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br>
</div>

<div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We have designed our marketing strategy to include advertising efforts in multiple media avenues such as television airtime on golf related events, product education for the consumer through an internet website, publications including periodicals and brochures, and in store media such as point of purchase displays and product introduction fact sheets.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December 31, 2010 and 2009, we spent approximately $4.0 million and $3.9 million, respectively, on the above listed marketing efforts.&#160;&#160;There can be no assurances that our marketing strategy will be effective or that increases in the levels of investments in advertising spending will result in material fluctuations in the sales of our products.</font></div>
